title: 第19章 大比前夕第20章 外门大比开幕
content_zh:
顾渊今夜睡不着。
他躺在稻草床上，眼睛睁着，盯着茅草屋顶的破洞。
月光从那个洞里漏下来，在泥地上投下一小片银白色的光斑，像是一枚被遗忘的银币。
胸口闷闷的。
不是印记的灼热——印记最近几天一直很安静，像是一头沉睡的野兽，在黑暗中积蓄着力量。
而是一种更微妙的、更难以名状的感觉。
像是有什么东西堵在心口，不疼痛，不难受，只是让他无法入睡。
顾渊知道那是什么。
明天。
外门大比。
他翻了个身，稻草在体重下发出细碎的摩擦声。
闭上眼睛，数呼吸。
一百下。
两百下。
数到三百的时候，他放弃了。
睡不着。
不是因为紧张，不是因为恐惧。
是因为某种更深的东西——一种他无法命名、但确实存在的情绪，像是有什么重要的东西即将发生，而他必须醒着等待。
他从稻草床上坐起来，系好草鞋，从床底摸出铁剑，推门走了出去。
夜已经很深了。

杂役院的弟子们都睡了，茅草屋里传来此起彼伏的鼾声和梦话。
食堂的方向一片漆黑，只有灶膛里未熄灭的炭火偶尔发出一丝微弱的红光，像是一只闭合的眼睛。
顾渊走向后院。
他的脚步很轻，像是怕惊动什么。
不是怕惊醒别人——杂役院的弟子们睡得死沉，天塌了都不一定醒得来。他是怕惊动自己心中那个正在慢慢成形的东西。
月光很亮，将雪地照成一片银白色的平原。
他的影子被拉得很长，投在雪地上，像是一个瘦长的幽灵跟着他走。
后院很安静。
石锁和木桩的影子在月光下显得格外清晰，像是被刀刻出来的剪影。顾渊走到演武场中央，那个他已经踩出凹陷的位置，站定，拔剑。
月光照在剑身上，将斑驳的剑身镀上一层银白色的光。
那道裂痕在月光下泛着一丝微弱的银白——和月光的颜色几乎一样。
顾渊深吸一口气，开始挥剑。
起势、蓄势、引势、发力、穿透、收势、回气、破空。
“铮。“
剑尖发出一声轻啸，白色气痕从剑尖射出，在雪地上划出一道清晰的痕迹。
这一剑很稳，比平时更稳——因为在挥剑的那一瞬间，他的心变得安静了。
顾渊一剑接一剑地挥着。
不是为了一万次的定额，不是为了精进剑技，只是为了让心安静下来。
一百剑。
两百剑。

三百剑。
月光慢慢移动，从东边移到西边，从头顶移到山脊。
顾渊的影子在地上旋转，从长变短，又从短变长。
在挥剑的间隙，他的脑海中浮现出一些画面。
content_en:
Gu Yuan couldn't sleep tonight.
He lay on his bed of straw, eyes open, staring at the holes in the thatched roof.
The moonlight leaked from the hole, casting a small silvery white spot on the dirt, like a forgotten silver coin.
Chest feels tight.
It's not the burning heat of the mark - the mark has been quiet in recent days, like a sleeping beast, gathering strength in the darkness.
But a subtler, more indescribable feeling.
It was like there was something stuck in his heart. It wasn't painful or uncomfortable, but it just kept him from falling asleep.
Gu Yuan knew what it was.
tomorrow.
Great competition at the outer door.
He turned over, the straw making a tiny scraping sound under his weight.
Close your eyes and count your breaths.
One hundred blows.
Two hundred blows.
When he counted to three hundred, he gave up.
Can't sleep.
Not out of nervousness, not out of fear.
It was because of something deeper—an emotion he couldn't name, but it was there, like something important was about to happen and he had to stay awake and wait.
He sat up from the straw bed, tied up his straw sandals, took out the iron sword from under the bed, opened the door and walked out.
The night is already very deep.
The disciples in the courtyard were all asleep, and snoring and talking in sleep came one after another from the thatched hut.
It was dark in the direction of the cafeteria, with only the unextinguished charcoal fire in the stove occasionally emitting a faint red light, like a closed eye.
Gu Yuan walked towards the backyard.
His steps were very light, as if he was afraid of disturbing anything.
It's not that they're afraid of waking others up - the disciples in the Miscellaneous Yard are so soundly asleep that they might not be able to wake up even if the sky falls. He was afraid of disturbing the thing that was slowly taking shape in his heart.
The moonlight was very bright, illuminating the snow into a silvery white plain.
His shadow was stretched out on the snow, like a lanky ghost following him.
The backyard is quiet.
The shadows of the stone locks and wooden stakes were particularly clear in the moonlight, like silhouettes carved by a knife. Gu Yuan walked to the center of the martial arts arena, where he had stepped out of the depression, stood still, and drew his sword.
The moonlight shines on the sword, coating the mottled sword with a layer of silvery white light.
The crack glowed with a faint silvery white under the moonlight - almost the same color as the moonlight.
Gu Yuan took a deep breath and began to swing his sword.
Starting momentum, accumulating momentum, leading momentum, exerting force, penetrating, closing momentum, returning energy, and breaking through.
"Zheng."
The tip of the sword let out a slight whistle, and white air marks shot out from the tip of the sword, leaving a clear mark on the snow.
This sword was very stable, more stable than usual - because the moment he swung the sword, his heart became quiet.
Gu Yuan swung his sword one after another.
Not for the quota of 10,000 times, not for improving sword skills, but just to calm down my heart.
One hundred swords.
Two hundred swords.
Three hundred swords.
The moonlight moved slowly, from east to west, from overhead to the ridge.
Gu Yuan's shadow rotated on the ground, changing from long to short, and then from short to long.
Between swings of the sword, some images appeared in his mind.
